content.text:
This confirms this is the commit that consolidated per-type reservation classes into a single `XReservation` with a switch statement, and introduced the copy-paste bug (all cases using `Individual` properties).

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 18f154d85110c36f6eb403d0a33703db4cfe8175

## Reasoning

(1) **Investigation**: I ran `git log --follow -p --reverse` on `XReservation.java` to see the full history of the file, including when the buggy switch-statement block (using `ReservationPriorityIndividual`, etc. for all reservation types) was first introduced.

(2) **Specific change**: Commit `18f154d8` (Dec 5, 2014) refactored several separate reservation classes (`XCourseReservation`, `XCurriculumReservation`, `XGroupReservation`, `XIndividualReservation`, `XDummyReservation`) into a single `XReservation` base class with a `switch` statement that sets priority/flags based on reservation type. In this refactor, the `Group`, `Curriculum`, and `Course` cases were mistakenly all set to use `ReservationPriorityIndividual`/`ReservationCanOverLimitIndividual`/etc. instead of their own type-specific properties (`...Group`, `...Curriculum`, `...Course`) — a clear copy-paste error, since the corresponding `ApplicationProperty` fields for Group/Curriculum/Course already existed (added in the same commit, per the diff stat showing 90 lines added to `ApplicationProperty.java`).

(3) **Evidence**: The diff of the fix commit (`6eb8807d`) exactly reverses this mistake — it changes `Group`, `Curriculum`, and `Course` cases from using `*Individual` properties to their respective `*Group`, `*Curriculum`, `*Course` properties, with no other logic changes. The `git log -p` history shows these four cases (Individual/Group/Curriculum/Course) were introduced together in `18f154d8` with all four branches identically referencing `*Individual` properties — confirming this was the point where the bug was created, and it persisted unnoticed from Dec 2014 until the fix in Feb 2016.

I'm highly confident in this identification, as the history is linear and unambiguous: no other commit touched this switch block between introduction and fix.
